Q: chdir syscall doesnt change my current directory A:

If you read the man page more carefully, you will see it also says:

The chdir() function only affects the working directory of the current process.

So, your program is updating only its own PWD. Every process has its own environment, so the PWD of the process that spawned your program is unaffected. This is why you don't see a new PWD in effect in your system's terminal after your program has exited.

Since you want to write your own Shell, you would likely have to also write your own terminal window as well. That way, commands entered into your terminal would affect data inside of your process. That is how you implement your own cd command using chdir() in its implementation.
